items.note: RCT with 305 MBA students that varies whether LLM support comes at problem formulation or only at ideation and evaluation; outcomes are the number (fluency) and strategic focus of alternatives generated. Abstract from Crossref (SSRN record).

Four online experiments (total N = 3,562; per-study N not in abstract) in which people collaborate with GenAI or work alone, then do a later task solo; abstract reports task performance and intrinsic motivation, and the search notes say tasks include alternative uses and product ideas rated for novelty and usefulness (possible after_ai outcome).

2x2 between-subjects design with 176 university students (same- vs cross-discipline groups, with vs without GenAI) measuring individual and group creativity; abstract only from the EdUHK repository via web search (Springer, OpenAlex, Crossref, S2 failed); a correction notice exists (10.1007/s10639-025-13878-x).

Exploratory classroom quasi-experiment: 27 students in seven self-selected teams, four of which used a GenAI plus XR pipeline; a seven-member panel rated team design presentations (quality, not explicitly creativity), with no significant difference; below 50 participants and non-random.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, S2, Crossref, Europe PMC, ScienceDirect and SSRN all failed); search notes describe a mixed-design team ideation experiment varying AI content strategy (breadth vs depth) and participation style with N = 52 (unverified), comparing AI configurations; SSRN version 10.2139/ssrn.5246400 is the same work.

Students in fine arts, literary writing and fashion design split equally into ChatGPT-4 intervention and standard-program control groups; creative thinking measured with the TTCT-Figural pre and post, a test taken without AI (after_ai); N not in abstract and assignment method not stated.

Controlled experiment comparing a ControlNet sketch-scaffolding workflow with static moodboard ideation among design students; blind experts rated line-art outcomes (higher design quality, d = 0.88); the sample size is missing from the OpenAlex abstract (blank parenthesis).

System paper (Scanvas) with a user study of 12 professional designers comparing the system with LLM ideation baselines on concept quality and synergy; AI-versus-AI comparison, no no-AI arm, far below 50 participants.

Two-stage design comparing Human-Only, LLM-Only and LLM-Assisted writing on originality and effectiveness; the LLM-Assisted versus Human-Only contrast may qualify, but much of the paper is an AI-versus-human comparison; N and assignment not in abstract.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, S2, Crossref, Europe PMC, ScienceDirect, web search); title indicates an empirical study of AI's effect on creativity in L1 Chinese writing, design unknown; classified experiment for full-text check.
